Work from home? Your rent isn't a write-off. Your office square feet might be.
This is for the self-employed. The space must be your main place of business, or used only for business and to meet clients regularly.
Say your apartment is one thousand square feet. Your office room is one hundred and twenty.
Rent, utilities, insurance: twenty thousand two hundred a year.
Twelve percent of that is two thousand, four hundred and twenty-four. That's your deduction.
In our sixty-thousand-dollar Manitoba example, that's about eight hundred and sixty dollars of tax and C-P-P saved.
Kitchen table? If the space is also personal, you cut the claim again, by the hours it's used for business.
And it can't create a business loss. The extra carries forward to next year.
Own your home? Claiming depreciation on the office can cost you when you sell. Get advice first.
Your home isn't the write-off. Your workspace is.
